product_from_film: Okara presents itself as private AI chat that lets a person use AI without exposing their work to an imagined data auction.
explains_well: The glass-room auction turns personal data exposure into a visible scene; opening Okara removes the writer and his desk from the auction display.
unclear: The film explains the privacy promise through a metaphor but gives no concrete view of which chat data is protected or what the privacy boundary includes.
scenario: Private conversations, interests and work appear as auction lots until a writer opens Okara and leaves the visible auction space.
product_clear_basis: The browser reaches okara.ai with a Private AI Chat tab title at 85s; the ending explicitly says AI that respects your privacy.

closer_windows.resolved: After the Okara browser view at 85–85.25s, the writer and desk remain in the glass room through about 86s, then the room is empty by 86.25s. The audience stays; a bright home typing view follows at about 89.75s. Exact compositing and easing are unverified.

categories.finding: Private exchange → data auction across several contexts → writer opens Okara → empty display → private home.
An intimate hand/sofa/phone scene begins before the surveillance context is revealed.
People using AI for private personal or work material are implied; private AI chat becomes explicit near 85s.
Repeated bids, scanned-looking scene representations and the writer’s disappearance carry the mechanism visually. A 4fps check places the empty-room change around 86–86.25s.
The glass room and seated audience persist across personal, nature, business, lab and writing contexts. The unchanged room after the writer vanishes makes the ending legible.
Cold dark auction scenes and occasional red states contrast with the final warm daylight room. The orange lamp links the writer’s two settings.
Little explanatory text appears during the metaphor; browser title, URL, BID ENDED and the final privacy line are key anchors.
ASR supports private conversation and auction descriptions. Heard voices, delivery and sound design are unknown.
Music character and structure are unverified.
Effects and their sources are unverified.

categories.finding: Sound sync is unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening or paired audiovisual timing.

categories.finding: Staged-looking rooms, bidders, data monitors, scanned scene graphics and a filmed browser form a cinematic metaphor. Production methods are unverified.
Source duration 105.958 s; Watch metadata 1920 × 1080. Frame rate, audio clipping and export quality not checked here.
categories.reason: Parent source metadata supports duration and dimensions; visual review is sampled.

categories.finding: Bidding paddles and data screens make exposure visible, but the precise data meaning depends partly on the draft. Product category arrives late.
The glass structure frames each subject as an object of attention; bidders and profile screens reinforce that focus.
The film spends about 85s building the auction threat before the product page and roughly 20s resolving it.
Opening Okara is followed by the writer disappearing from the display and continuing at home, a clear metaphorical payoff.
Intimate scenes exposed to bidders suggest discomfort; warm home imagery suggests relief. Audience response and audio performance are unmeasured.
The same glass-room auction rule applies to each context, then breaks for the writer using Okara.
The auction is a metaphor, not evidence of actual data sales by any provider. Okara’s privacy properties and chat behavior are not independently established.
Removing the entire writer/desk from an otherwise unchanged auction room makes privacy visible without a technical diagram.
Add a concise statement of the actual protection boundary.
categories.experiment: Show one chat example beside a plain statement of what is stored, shared or excluded, using verified product facts.

categories.finding: For Tin, let the closing action visibly resolve the opening visual rule.
categories.experiment: Show a campaign trapped in repeated manual reviews, then one approved workflow moving it to a clearly published state.

categories.reason: The product summary is this model’s film-only reading.

lessons.keep: Build a repeated visual rule and let the product action break it.
try: Add a plain, verified statement of the chat privacy boundary.
For Tin, resolve a repeated manual-review image with one visible published outcome.
lessons.avoid: Treating the auction metaphor as factual evidence of data sales or privacy implementation.
lessons.open: Exact privacy scope, chat behavior, visual production methods and audio qualities remain unverified.

comparison.story: Personal/work data auction → private chat choice → escape into home.
comparison.motion: Repeated room substitutions and a checked disappearance around 86s.
comparison.sound: ASR supports auction roles; no validated listening.
comparison.texture: Dark glass enclosures against warm domestic daylight.
comparison.lesson: A visual metaphor can make an abstract promise memorable, but the actual boundary still needs words.
